nuggets.title: Late CRM row creates overlapping SCD2 intervals

scenario.symptoms: Customer dimension queries for ‘as of March 15’ return two active addresses. A CRM correction effective February 10 arrived on March 20 and was inserted without closing the March 1 version.
scenario.interviewerSetup: SCD2 loader appends new rows using load date instead of source effective date and skips interval repair for late records.

incident.headline: Late-arriving change fails to split historical validity intervals

agenda.goal: Maintain non-overlapping SCD2 timelines when corrections arrive late.
agenda.opener: Two active addresses exist for one point in time—how should the loader handle a late CRM correction?

evidence.strong: Use source effective timestamps, locate overlapping interval, close prior row valid_to, insert corrected row, ripple forward if needed.
evidence.adequate: Insert new current row only, leaving history wrong.
evidence.weak: Append row with load timestamp as valid_from.

misconceptions.pattern: Using pipeline run time as valid_from.
misconceptions.challenge: Change happened in February but loaded in March—what should valid_from be?

probes: How do you detect overlapping valid_from/valid_to?
What happens to facts pointing at surrogate keys during splits?
agenda.referenceFix: Apply corrections by source effective date: close affected row at effective instant, insert new version, adjust subsequent intervals, and validate no overlaps via constraints.

nuggets.title: Daily load creates duplicate SCD2 versions

scenario.symptoms: Customer dimension row count grew 40% month-over-month though business changes were flat. Nightly extracts re-insert identical rows because change detection compares all columns including volatile audit fields.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Loader treats any column difference as a new version; source sends unchanged attributes plus updated_at metadata each day.

incident.headline: Noisy change detection generates spurious SCD2 history rows

agenda.goal: Open a new SCD2 version only when tracked attributes truly change.
agenda.opener: Dimension history exploded without real business changes—how do you detect genuine changes?

evidence.strong: Hash tracked business columns, ignore volatile metadata, compare hash to active version, skip insert when equal.
evidence.adequate: Compare dozens of columns individually without hash.

misconceptions.pattern: Inserting on every extract schedule tick.
misconceptions.challenge: If address unchanged for 30 days, should you have 30 versions?

probes: Which columns belong in the hash?
How does hash compare scale versus wide rows?
hints: Exclude source updated_at from business hash.
agenda.referenceFix: Compute row hash over tracked attributes only, compare to current active hash, and insert/close versions solely when hash differs.

nuggets.title: GDPR delete leaves PII in history

scenario.symptoms: Privacy request verified removal from the active customer row, but analysts still queried historical SCD2 versions containing email and phone from prior years.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Erasure job updates is_current flag and deletes active row attributes but historical versions remain untouched.

incident.headline: GDPR job masks current row but leaves PII in SCD2 history

agenda.goal: Honor erasure across all historical dimension versions without breaking facts.
agenda.opener: User was ‘deleted’ but old dimension rows still show email—how do you erase SCD2 history safely?

evidence.strong: Mask/hash PII on all versions, retain surrogate key for facts, optional cryptoshred, audit trail of erasure.
evidence.adequate: Delete all history rows and orphan facts.

misconceptions.challenge: What happens to sales facts referencing the surrogate key?

probes: Which fields can be nulled vs must remain for analytics?
How do you prove erasure completeness?
hints: Apply masking to every version row.
agenda.referenceFix: Run erasure across all SCD2 versions for the business key: replace PII with irreversible tokens, keep surrogate key and non-PII attributes, log completion, and validate with automated scans.
